source.role: Exact English curriculum objectives, roleplays, terms and Reader lines retained as provenance; Japanese learner scenes use original contextual wording and aligned English support

sourceEnglish.objective: greet staff, learn whether to order at the counter, and find a place
sourceEnglish.roleplay: Walk into a crowded Roman café and work out how ordering and seating operate.
englishWordAnchors: Good morning, do I order here at the counter?
Do I sit wherever I want?
Sorry, I don't understand. Can you repeat, please?
Is it to go or to eat here?
englishReading: A traveler enters a very busy café.
There is a long line in front of the counter.
The traveler says: Good morning.
He asks the waitress: Do I order here at the counter?
The waitress answers: Yes, order here, please.
He asks: Is there a free table?
The waitress says: There is a table on the patio.
He waits in line and looks at the menu.
Then he orders a coffee and a sweet pastry.

lessons.title: Entering a busy café
lessons.objective: Greet staff, ask whether to order at the counter, and find out if a seat is available.
lessons.focus: In a Japanese café, counter and seating practices vary. 注文はここでいいですか asks where to order. 空いていますか asks whether a seat is free. Check with staff rather than sitting or assuming a universal rule.
lessons.scene: Sam enters a busy café near a station and asks the staff how to order.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: 駅の近くのカフェは混んでいます。
reader.en: The café near the station is busy.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: カウンターの前に列があります。
reader.en: There is a line in front of the counter.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: おはようございます。注文はここでいいですか。
reader.en: Good morning. Should I order here?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい、こちらでご注文ください。
reader.en: Yes, please order here.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 席は空いていますか。
reader.en: Is a seat available?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 窓の近くに一つ空いています。
reader.en: One seat near the window is available.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: わかりました。少し待ちます。
reader.en: I understand. I will wait a moment.

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: サムはメニューを見て、列で待ちます。
reader.en: Sam looks at the menu and waits in line.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: コーヒーを一杯ください。
reader.en: One coffee, please.

speaking.opening: いらっしゃいませ。ご注文ですか。
speaking.goal: Greet staff, ask where to order, then ask whether a seat is available.
speaking.closure: Follow the staff’s actual instructions; do not assume counter service everywhere.

modes.say: Ask staff where to order and whether there is a seat.

sourceEnglish.objective: ask about coffee styles, size, milk, temperature, and where to drink it
sourceEnglish.roleplay: Order a local coffee without assuming the names or customs are the same as at home.
englishWordAnchors: What types of coffee are there?
I want a coffee with milk, please.
Is it to drink here or to go?
englishReading: A traveler arrives at the counter of a café.
She asks: What types of coffee are there?
The barista says there is black coffee and coffee with milk.
She wants a medium coffee with milk.
She asks: Do you have oat milk?
The barista answers yes, and asks if she wants it hot or cold.
She asks for the coffee hot and asks: Is it to drink here or to go?
She takes a table and drinks her coffee.

lessons.title: Choosing a coffee
lessons.objective: Ask what coffee is offered, check milk and size options, then state whether you will drink it there.
lessons.focus: ブレンド and アメリカン are menu labels, not universal translations of black coffee. Ask what a shop offers. 牛乳 and オーツミルク are ingredients, but availability and allergy safety require confirmation. ～にできますか asks whether a change is possible.
lessons.scene: Sam studies a café menu and checks which milk and size are available.

cards.ja: どんなコーヒーがありますか
オーツミルクはありますか
温かいものをお願いします

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: どんなコーヒーがありますか。
reader.en: What coffees do you have?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: ブレンドとカフェオレがあります。
reader.en: We have blend coffee and café au lait.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: カフェオレは小さいサイズがありますか。
reader.en: Is there a small café au lait?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい、あります。
reader.en: Yes, there is.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: オーツミルクはありますか。
reader.en: Do you have oat milk?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 今日はありません。牛乳ならあります。
reader.en: We do not have it today. We have milk.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: では、小さいブレンドを温かいものでお願いします。
reader.en: Then a small hot blend coffee, please.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 店内でお召し上がりですか。
reader.en: Will you drink it here?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: はい、店内で飲みます。
reader.en: Yes, I will drink it here.

speaking.opening: ご注文は何になさいますか。
speaking.goal: Ask about coffee choices, size and milk availability; order a hot drink for here.
speaking.closure: Repeat only options the barista confirmed.
wordBank: どんなコーヒーがありますか

modes.see: Read a coffee-choice scene and reveal accurate English support.
modes.recall: Recall milk, size and temperature terms.
modes.hear: Hear 温かい versus 冷たい.
modes.type: Type an availability question with kana support.
modes.say: Ask about coffee and milk, then place an order.
modes.write: Write a short order with confirmed size and temperature.

sourceEnglish.objective: ask what is fresh, filled, sweet, savory, or typical
sourceEnglish.roleplay: Ask the server to explain three pastries and recommend one made that morning.
englishWordAnchors: Which one is the most typical?
Which one came out of the oven today?
englishReading: A traveler walks into a bakery in the morning.
There are many breads and pastries on the counter.
He asks: What is fresh today?
The employee says the sweet bread is from this morning.
The traveler asks: Which one is filled?
She explains that the concha is sweet and the empanada is savory.
He says: I want to try something typical from here.
The employee recommends a bolillo with cheese.
The traveler orders a concha and a coffee, please.

lessons.title: Choosing a pastry
lessons.objective: Ask what was baked this morning, whether an item is filled, and which pastry the staff recommends.
lessons.focus: 今朝焼いたもの asks what was baked this morning; it does not certify freshness, ingredients or safety. 甘い and 塩味のある distinguish sweet and savory. 中身 refers to a filling. Pastry names vary by café, so use menu labels actually shown.
lessons.scene: At a bakery café, Sam asks about three pastries without inventing what they contain.

cards.ja: 今朝焼いたものはどれですか
どれをおすすめしますか

reader.speaker: Narrator
reader.ja: サムはパン屋のカウンターを見ます。
reader.en: Sam looks at the bakery counter.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 今朝焼いたものはどれですか。
reader.en: Which items were baked this morning?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: このクロワッサンとあんパンです。
reader.en: This croissant and anpan were.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: あんパンの中身は何ですか。
reader.en: What is inside the anpan?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: あんこです。甘いですよ。
reader.en: Sweet bean paste. It is sweet.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 塩味のあるものはありますか。
reader.en: Do you have something savory?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: このチーズパンがあります。
reader.en: We have this cheese bread.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: どれをおすすめしますか。
reader.en: Which do you recommend?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 今朝焼いたクロワッサンをおすすめします。
reader.en: I recommend the croissant baked this morning.

speaking.opening: いらっしゃいませ。何かお探しですか。
speaking.goal: Ask which items were baked this morning, ask about a filling, and request a recommendation.
speaking.closure: Treat the staff answer as a menu description, not an allergen guarantee.

modes.see: Read a bakery counter scene with aligned English support.
modes.recall: Recall baked-today, filling, sweet and savory forms.
modes.hear: Hear 甘い versus 塩味のある.
modes.type: Type a short filling question with kana help.
modes.say: Ask about three pastries and request a recommendation.
modes.write: Write a question about baking time and a recommendation request.

sourceEnglish.objective: request eggs, sides, toast, fruit, and cooking preferences
sourceEnglish.roleplay: Build a complete hot breakfast order and confirm what is included.
englishWordAnchors: I want two scrambled eggs, please.
englishReading: A traveler walks into a café in the morning.
He sits at a table and looks at the menu.
The waitress asks: What would you like?
He says: I want two scrambled eggs, please.
He also orders bacon, toast, and fruit.
The waitress asks: How do you want the eggs?
He answers: I want them well done, without salt.
Then he asks: Is the coffee included?
The waitress says: Yes, the coffee is included.

lessons.title: Ordering a full breakfast
lessons.objective: Order eggs and sides, state a cooking preference, and ask which items are included.
lessons.focus: ～をお願いします makes a polite order. 焼き加減 means cooking level; よく焼いてください requests well cooked. セットに含まれますか checks whether something is included. Menu contents and cooking choices vary; do not imply a fixed breakfast set.
lessons.scene: Sam sees an egg breakfast set on a café menu and asks what comes with it.

cards.ja: セットに含まれますか
cards.en: Is it included in the set?

cards.ja: 塩なしでお願いします

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: この朝食セットには何が付きますか。
reader.en: What comes with this breakfast set?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 卵料理とトーストと果物が付きます。
reader.en: It comes with an egg dish, toast, and fruit.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 卵料理は選べますか。
reader.en: Can I choose the egg dish?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい、目玉焼きかスクランブルエッグです。
reader.en: Yes, fried or scrambled eggs.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: スクランブルエッグをお願いします。
reader.en: Scrambled eggs, please.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: よく焼いてください。
reader.en: Please cook them well.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: かしこまりました。
reader.en: Certainly.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: コーヒーもセットに含まれますか。
reader.en: Is coffee included in the set too?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: いいえ、コーヒーは別料金です。
reader.en: No, coffee costs extra.

speaking.opening: 朝食セットはいかがですか。
speaking.goal: Ask what is included, choose an egg dish, state a cooking preference, and check whether coffee costs extra.
speaking.closure: Repeat the staff’s answer without assuming all breakfast sets are the same.

modes.see: Read a breakfast-set exchange with aligned English.
modes.recall: Recall egg dishes, sides and included-price questions.
modes.hear: Hear the distinction between 目玉焼き and スクランブルエッグ.
modes.type: Type a cooking preference with kana help.
modes.say: Order an egg set and ask what comes with it.
modes.write: Write a short order plus an inclusion question.

sourceEnglish.objective: ask whether breakfast is included, the hours, room number, and buffet rules
sourceEnglish.roleplay: Arrive at a hotel breakfast and resolve uncertainty about access and seating.
englishWordAnchors: Can I sit at any table?
Excuse me, what are the buffet rules?
englishReading: A traveler arrives at the hotel dining room in the morning.
He talks to the receptionist: Is breakfast included?
She says: Yes, it is included with your room.
He asks: What are the breakfast hours?
She answers that the hours are from 6:30 to 10:00, according to the hotel.
The traveler gives his room number: 214.
Then he asks: Is it a buffet or a menu?
She explains the buffet rules: take a clean plate and do not take food with you.
He looks for a free table and gets coffee.

lessons.title: Checking hotel breakfast
lessons.objective: Ask whether your room plan includes breakfast, confirm the hours, and ask how the buffet works.
lessons.focus: 朝食付き means breakfast included in a particular booking; it is not assumed. 何時から何時まで asks the hours. 部屋番号 is room number. Follow the hotel’s stated buffet rules rather than treating one hotel’s practice as universal.
lessons.scene: At the hotel dining-room entrance, Sam gives a room number and checks the booking.

cards.en: from what time to what time

cards.ja: ルールを教えてください

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: おはようございます。朝食はこちらですか。
reader.en: Good morning. Is breakfast here?

reader.speaker: Host
reader.ja: はい。お部屋番号をお願いします。
reader.en: Yes. Your room number, please.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 二一四号室です。
reader.en: Room 214.

reader.speaker: Host
reader.ja: 宿泊プランを確認します。
reader.en: I will check your room plan.

reader.speaker: Host
reader.ja: 朝食付きのプランです。
reader.en: Your plan includes breakfast.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 朝食は何時から何時までですか。
reader.en: What are the breakfast hours?

reader.speaker: Host
reader.ja: 六時半から十時までです。
reader.en: From six thirty to ten.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: ビュッフェのルールを教えてください。
reader.en: Please explain the buffet rules.

reader.speaker: Host
reader.ja: こちらで新しいお皿をお取りください。
reader.en: Please take a clean plate here.

speaking.opening: おはようございます。お部屋番号をお願いします。
speaking.goal: Provide a room number, ask whether the booked plan includes breakfast, confirm hours and ask about buffet rules.
speaking.closure: Follow only the host’s stated rules for this hotel.

modes.say: Check breakfast access and ask about rules.
modes.write: Write room number, inclusion and hours questions.

sourceEnglish.objective: state an allergy or dietary need and confirm ingredients without seeking medical advice
sourceEnglish.roleplay: Ask whether a breakfast item contains nuts, dairy, gluten, meat, or another ingredient.
englishWordAnchors: I have an allergy to nuts.
Can you check with the kitchen, please?
englishReading: I am in a café and I talk to the server before ordering.
First I say: I have an allergy to nuts.
Then I ask: What ingredients does it have?
The server is not sure, so he is going to check with the kitchen.
Afterward he tells me that, according to the kitchen, the bread has no nuts.
I also say: I don't eat meat, and I ask if the filling has meat in it.
If the kitchen is not sure, I order something else.
I only confirm the ingredients and I do not ask for medical advice.

lessons.title: State a food restriction
lessons.objective: Tell staff about a nut allergy or food preference, ask the kitchen to check ingredients and handling, and decline when the answer is uncertain.
lessons.focus: アレルギーがあります states an allergy; 肉を食べません states a preference and must not be conflated. 原材料 asks about ingredients; 調理器具 asks about utensils and possible shared handling. A statement that an ingredient is absent does not prove a dish is safe. If staff cannot confirm, do not order that dish. This language is a communication draft pending qualified food-allergy review, not medical advice.
lessons.scene: Sam asks about a pastry for a companion with a nut allergy; staff cannot verify its preparation.

cards.ja: ナッツアレルギーがあります

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: すみません。同行者にナッツアレルギーがあります。
reader.en: Excuse me. My companion has a nut allergy.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: このパンの原材料を確認していただけますか。
reader.en: Could you check the ingredients of this bread?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 厨房に確認します。少々お待ちください。
reader.en: I will check with the kitchen. Please wait a moment.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 原材料は確認できましたが、調理器具は共用です。
reader.en: We checked the ingredients, but the cooking utensils are shared.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 詳しい取り扱いは確認できますか。
reader.en: Can you confirm how it is handled in detail?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 申し訳ありません。そこまでは確認できません。
reader.en: I am sorry. I cannot confirm that.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: わかりました。このパンは注文しません。
reader.en: I understand. I will not order this bread.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 承知しました。
reader.en: Understood.

speaking.opening: ご注文はお決まりですか。
speaking.goal: State the companion’s allergy, request an ingredient and handling check, and decline the item if staff cannot verify it.
speaking.closure: Do not interpret an ingredient list alone as proof of safety; this practice scenario is not medical advice.
wordBank: 確認していただけますか

modes.see: Read the restriction scene with aligned English.
modes.recall: Distinguish an allergy from a food preference.
modes.hear: Hear 確認できます and 確認できません.
modes.type: Type an ingredient-check request with kana support.
modes.say: State a restriction and ask for verification without assuming safety.
modes.write: Write a brief restriction statement and a decline when facts are uncertain.

sourceEnglish.objective: ask for a typical regional breakfast and understand a cultural explanation
sourceEnglish.roleplay: Tell the server you want the breakfast locals actually choose, not a tourist substitute.
englishWordAnchors: What do people here eat for breakfast?
I want the breakfast that locals order.
I don't want something just for tourists.
Can you recommend a typical dish to me?
Can you explain to me what it has in it?
Can you repeat that more slowly, please?
englishReading: Ana sits at a table in a small café in Puebla.
First she asks the server: What do people here eat for breakfast?
Then she says: I want the breakfast that locals order.
The server smiles and says that chilaquiles are a typical morning dish.
According to him, they are going to serve the chilaquiles with green salsa and beans.
Ana asks: Can you explain to me what it has in it?
The server explains that café de olla comes with cinnamon and that the sweet bread is for afterward.
Ana orders the chilaquiles, a café de olla, and a sweet bread.
At the end, she is going to pay at the counter.

lessons.title: Ask about a local breakfast
lessons.objective: Ask staff what people in the area choose for breakfast, hear the explanation, and check the ingredients before ordering.
lessons.focus: この辺りでは means around here; この店では means at this shop. 「地元の人は」 asks about local customers without claiming everyone eats the same thing. A recommendation is one staff member’s description, not a universal cultural fact or ingredient guarantee.
lessons.scene: Sam asks a café worker which breakfast on this shop’s menu is popular with local customers.

cards.ja: この店では何が人気ですか
cards.en: What is popular at this shop?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: この辺りでは、朝食に何を食べますか。
reader.en: What do people around here eat for breakfast?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 人によりますが、この店ではおにぎり定食が人気です。
reader.en: It depends on the person, but the rice-ball set is popular here.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 何が付きますか。
reader.en: What comes with it?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: おにぎりと味噌汁と漬物が付きます。
reader.en: It comes with rice balls, miso soup, and pickles.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: おにぎりの中身は何ですか。
reader.en: What is inside the rice balls?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 今日の中身は鮭です。
reader.en: Today the filling is salmon.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 材料をもう少し教えていただけますか。
reader.en: Could you tell me a little more about the ingredients?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 厨房に確認します。
reader.en: I will check with the kitchen.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: ありがとうございます。確認をお願いします。
reader.en: Thank you. Please check.

speaking.opening: おはようございます。メニューをご覧になりますか。
speaking.goal: Ask about a local breakfast choice, what comes with it, and the ingredients before ordering.
speaking.closure: Wait for any kitchen check; do not generalize one menu item to all Japanese breakfasts.

modes.see: Read the shop recommendation with English support.
modes.recall: Recall local-area, set meal and ingredient questions.
modes.hear: Hear おにぎり and 味噌汁 in context.
modes.type: Type a short recommendation question with kana help.
modes.say: Ask what locals order and what is in one item.
modes.write: Write a recommendation question and an ingredient check.

sourceEnglish.objective: order several drinks and foods accurately and confirm who gets each item
sourceEnglish.roleplay: Order breakfast for a family or group with different preferences.
englishWordAnchors: I want to order for everyone, please.
Can you repeat the order, please?
englishReading: I am in a café with my wife, my son, and my mother-in-law.
First, I say to the waiter: I want to order for everyone, please.
For me, a coffee with milk and some scrambled eggs.
For my wife, a tea and a ham sandwich, without cheese.
My son is going to have orange juice and a sweet roll.
My mother-in-law wants a decaf coffee and toast with butter.
Then, I repeat the order: Is that correct? The tea is for her, right?
The waiter smiles and says: Everything is right, I'll bring it right away.
At the end, I ask for the check at the table.

lessons.title: Order for a group
lessons.objective: Order different drinks and foods for three people, then read back who receives each item.
lessons.focus: ～には marks the person receiving an item. それぞれ means each person. こちらは誰の分ですか asks whose portion an item is. Japanese often uses a person’s name rather than a bare pronoun. Avoid mixing an allergy need with an ordinary taste preference.
lessons.scene: Sam orders with two companions at a café and checks the server’s readback.

cards.ja: 注文を確認してください

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: ご注文をどうぞ。
reader.en: Please tell me your order.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 三人分をお願いします。
reader.en: An order for three people, please.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 私にはカフェオレと卵料理をお願いします。
reader.en: Coffee with milk and an egg dish for me, please.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 友人には紅茶とトーストをお願いします。
reader.en: Tea and toast for my friend, please.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 子どもにはオレンジジュースとパンをお願いします。
reader.en: Orange juice and bread for the child, please.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 確認します。カフェオレと卵料理はお客様の分ですね。
reader.en: Let me confirm. The coffee with milk and egg dish are for you.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: はい。紅茶とトーストは友人の分です。
reader.en: Yes. The tea and toast are for my friend.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: オレンジジュースとパンはお子様の分ですね。
reader.en: The orange juice and bread are for the child.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: はい、そのとおりです。
reader.en: Yes, that is correct.

speaking.goal: Place three distinct orders and confirm who receives each item.
speaking.closure: Read back the allocation before the server submits the order.
wordBank: 注文を確認してください

modes.recall: Recall who gets each food and drink.
modes.type: Type a short allocation sentence with kana help.
modes.say: Order for three and confirm the readback.

sourceEnglish.objective: ask for food or coffee to go, packaging, napkins, and utensils
sourceEnglish.roleplay: Convert part of a seated order into takeaway because your train leaves soon.
englishWordAnchors: Can I order the coffee to go?
I want this to go, please.
Can you give me napkins and a spoon?
Can you put it in a bag for me?
Does it come with a lid?
englishReading: A traveler is in a café and looks at the clock.
First he orders a coffee with milk and a croissant at the counter.
Then he says: Excuse me, can I order the coffee to go?
The waitress asks: Do you want a lid and a bag?
The traveler answers: Yes, please, and I also need napkins and a spoon.
After that he changes the croissant order, because he is going to eat on the train.
He says: Can you put it in a paper bag for me?
In the end he pays the bill and says thank you.
With his order in hand, he quickly heads out to the station.

lessons.title: Change part of an order to takeaway
lessons.objective: Ask to take a coffee and pastry away, check packaging, and request a napkin or spoon.
lessons.focus: 持ち帰り means takeaway. ～に変更できますか asks if a change is possible; do not assume a prepared order can be changed. 袋 is a bag and ふた is a lid. Ask whether these are supplied; packaging and train policies vary.
lessons.scene: Sam has limited time before a train and asks the café to change the unprepared part of an order.

cards.ja: 持ち帰りにできますか

cards.en: Please put it in a bag

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: すみません。電車の時間が近いです。
reader.en: Excuse me. My train time is close.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: コーヒーを持ち帰りに変更できますか。
reader.en: Can you change the coffee to takeaway?

reader.speaker: Staff

sourceEnglish.objective: politely identify a missing or incorrect item and request the right one
sourceEnglish.roleplay: You received the wrong coffee and one pastry is missing; resolve both without sounding hostile.
englishWordAnchors: Excuse me, I think there is a mistake with my order.
I ordered an americano, not a coffee with milk.
Can you change it for me, please?
Can you check my order, please?
englishReading: I get to the counter and order an americano and a pastry.
Then the server gives me a cup of coffee with milk.
I check my bag and see that there is no pastry in it.
First, I smile and say: Excuse me, I think there is a mistake with my order.
Then I explain: I ordered an americano, not a coffee with milk.
I also say: I am missing a pastry, and here is my receipt.
I ask: Can you change it for me, please?
The server says: Of course, I will bring you the coffee and the pastry now.

lessons.title: Correct an order politely
lessons.objective: Explain that the drink is different from what you ordered and a pastry is missing; offer the receipt so staff can check.
lessons.focus: 注文したのは～です identifies the item ordered. ～ではなく means not X but Y. 入っていません says an item is missing from a bag. Ask staff to check before asserting fault. Menu labels for アメリカン and ブレンド vary, so use the exact label shown on this order.
lessons.scene: Sam checks a takeaway bag and notices a different drink and missing pastry.

cards.ja: 注文したのはブレンドです
クロワッサンが入っていません

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: すみません。注文を確認していただけますか。
reader.en: Excuse me. Could you check my order?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい。どうなさいましたか。
reader.en: Yes. What seems to be the problem?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 注文したのはブレンドですが、これはカフェオレです。
reader.en: I ordered a blend coffee, but this is coffee with milk.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: クロワッサンも袋に入っていません。
reader.en: The croissant is not in the bag either.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: レシートはこちらです。
reader.en: Here is the receipt.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 確認します。少々お待ちください。
reader.en: I will check. Please wait a moment.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 失礼しました。ご注文を確認できました。
reader.en: I am sorry. We confirmed your order.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: ブレンドとクロワッサンをお持ちします。
reader.en: I will bring the blend coffee and croissant.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: ありがとうございます。
reader.en: Thank you.

speaking.closure: Wait for the verified correction; avoid blame.

sourceEnglish.objective: exchange greetings and talk briefly about the day, weather, and plans
sourceEnglish.roleplay: Chat naturally with a barista or nearby customer while waiting.
englishWordAnchors: Good morning, how are you this morning?
It is very cold today, isn't it?
I am still a little sleepy.
I am going to visit downtown if it does not rain.
Sorry, can you repeat that more slowly, please?
You too, have a good day!
englishReading: It is early and I am in a small café, waiting for my coffee with milk at the counter.
The barista smiles at me and says: Good morning, how are you this morning?
I answer: Very well, thanks, but I am still a little sleepy.
She comments that it is cold today because it rained last night, and I tell her the weather is very different in my country.
A man near me asks: What plans do you have for today?
I explain that I am going to visit downtown if it does not rain again.
He recommends that I bring a coat, because according to the forecast the afternoon is going to be cool.
When my order is ready, the barista tells me: Have a great day!
I answer with a smile: You too, have a good day!

lessons.title: Morning small talk
lessons.objective: Exchange a greeting, comment on the weather and share a tentative plan while waiting for a drink.
lessons.focus: 今日は寒いですね invites agreement about present weather. ～なら expresses a condition, as in 雨が降らなければ. Keep the exchange brief and appropriate with staff; do not claim a forecast unless someone actually reports it. Ask for repetition politely if needed.
lessons.scene: Sam makes brief small talk with a barista while waiting for a coffee.

cards.en: It is cold today, isn’t it?

reader.speaker: Barista
reader.ja: おはようございます。今日は寒いですね。
reader.en: Good morning. It is cold today, isn’t it?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: おはようございます。本当に寒いですね。
reader.en: Good morning. It really is cold.

reader.speaker: Barista
reader.ja: コーヒーはもう少しでできます。
reader.en: Your coffee will be ready shortly.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: ありがとうございます。まだ少し眠いです。
reader.en: Thank you. I am still a little sleepy.

reader.speaker: Barista
reader.ja: 今日はどちらへ行きますか。
reader.en: Where are you going today?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 雨が降らなければ、駅前を散歩します。
reader.en: If it does not rain, I will walk near the station.

reader.speaker: Barista
reader.ja: いいですね。こちらがコーヒーです。
reader.en: That sounds nice. Here is your coffee.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: ありがとうございます。よい一日を。
reader.en: Thank you. Have a good day.

reader.speaker: Barista
reader.ja: お客様も、よい一日を。
reader.en: You too. Have a good day.

sourceEnglish.objective: request the bill, understand cover or service charges, and choose a payment method
sourceEnglish.roleplay: Pay for breakfast, clarify one unfamiliar charge, and request a receipt.
englishWordAnchors: Could you bring me the bill, please?
I want to pay in cash.
Could you give me the receipt, please?
englishReading: After eating breakfast, the traveler raises his hand and says: Excuse me, could you bring me the bill, please?
The waitress answers that he can pay at the register or at the table, as he prefers.
When the bill arrives, the traveler sees an extra charge and asks: What is this charge?
The waitress explains that it is the cover charge, and that the menu states it on the last page.
The traveler says he understands, but he wants to know if the tip is included.
She answers that service is not included, so the tip is optional.
Since he has no cash, the traveler asks: Can I pay by card?
The waitress brings the card terminal, he pays, and he asks her for the receipt.
Before leaving, the traveler checks the total and says thank you.

lessons.title: Understand the bill
lessons.objective: Ask for the bill, clarify an unfamiliar item, confirm the total and payment method, then request a receipt.
lessons.focus: お会計 is the bill/payment; 明細 is the itemized detail; 合計 is the total. こちらの料金は何ですか asks about an unfamiliar charge without assuming a cover charge or tip applies. Payment methods, service charges and tipping practices vary; check the actual bill and staff answer.
lessons.scene: Sam checks a café bill that includes a separately listed drink and asks about it.

cards.ja: こちらの料金は何ですか

reader.speaker: Sam

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい。セットには含まれていません。
reader.en: Yes. It is not included in the set.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: わかりました。合計はいくらですか。
reader.en: I see. What is the total?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 合計は千二百円です。
reader.en: The total is twelve hundred yen.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: カードで払えますか。
reader.en: Can I pay by card?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい、レジで払えます。
reader.en: Yes, you can pay at the register.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: レシートもください。
reader.en: The receipt too, please.

speaking.goal: Ask about a separate charge, confirm the total and card payment, and request the receipt.
speaking.closure: Pay the confirmed amount; do not invent a universal service-charge or tip rule.

sourceEnglish.objective: give a specific, natural compliment and thank the staff warmly
sourceEnglish.roleplay: Tell the cook why the pastry or coffee was memorable rather than only saying it was good.
englishWordAnchors: I want to compliment you on the breakfast.
The coffee was delicious, just the way I like it.
I loved it because it was very soft.
Thank you very much for the service.
If I come back tomorrow, I'm going to order another one.
englishReading: A traveler finishes her breakfast in a small café and wants to talk to the cook.
She greets him and says: I want to compliment you on the breakfast.
The coffee was very strong and had a delicious aroma, just the way I like it.
The sweet bread was soft inside and crunchy outside, and it wasn't too sweet.
I also loved the eggs, because they were creamy and very well seasoned.
The cook smiles and explains that the sweet bread is his grandmother's recipe.
The traveler tells him: If I come back tomorrow, I'm going to order another one of those.
Before leaving, she leaves a tip on the counter and thanks the staff for the service.
The cook answers: Thank you very much, we're so glad you liked it.

lessons.title: A specific thank-you
lessons.objective: Give a specific compliment about coffee and pastry, then thank the staff without inventing a family recipe or tip custom.
lessons.focus: ～が香り高かったです describes an aromatic item after eating. 外はさくさく、中はふんわり gives a concrete texture contrast. おいしかったです is polite past. Staff access to the cook is not assumed; offer the compliment to the person serving you.
lessons.scene: After breakfast, Sam thanks café staff for a coffee and pastry.

reader.speaker: Staff

reader.speaker: Sam

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 作った方にも伝えていただけますか。

reader.speaker: Staff

reader.speaker: Sam

sourceEnglish.objective: explain time pressure, ask what is fastest, and confirm preparation time
sourceEnglish.roleplay: You have twelve minutes before a tour; ask for a realistic fast option.
englishWordAnchors: I'm in a hurry because my tour leaves soon.
What is the fastest thing you have?
How long does the preparation take?
Could it be to go, please?
Could you bring me the bill now, please?
englishReading: A traveler walks into a café at 8:00 and talks with the waitress at the counter.
He says: I'm in a hurry because my tour leaves in 12 minutes.
He asks: What is the fastest thing you have for breakfast?
The waitress answers that an egg sandwich and an americano come out quickly.
The traveler asks: How long does the sandwich take to prepare?
She says it takes about 5 minutes, according to the kitchen.
If it is possible, he wants breakfast to go, because he has no time to sit down.
He also asks for the bill now so he can pay at the counter.
The waitress smiles and says: My pleasure, I'll get it ready for you right away.

lessons.title: A rushed breakfast
lessons.objective: Explain a twelve-minute limit, ask what can be prepared quickly, and confirm the expected time before ordering.
lessons.focus: あと十二分です means twelve minutes remain. 何分くらいかかりますか asks an approximate preparation time. すぐできるもの asks what can be ready soon, but staff must answer. A quoted time is an estimate, not a guarantee; the traveler decides whether to order.
lessons.scene: Sam has a tour meeting soon and asks a café worker for a realistic breakfast option.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: すみません。ツアーまであと十二分です。
reader.en: Excuse me. I have twelve minutes before my tour.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: すぐできる朝食はありますか。
reader.en: Is there a breakfast that can be ready quickly?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: おにぎりなら、すぐお渡しできます。
reader.en: We can hand you a rice ball soon.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: サンドイッチは何分くらいかかりますか。
reader.en: About how many minutes would a sandwich take?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 五分くらいですが、混み具合で変わります。
reader.en: About five minutes, but it depends on how busy we are.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: では、おにぎりを持ち帰りでお願いします。
reader.en: Then a rice ball to take away, please.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: 先にお会計できますか。
reader.en: Can I pay first?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい、こちらでお願いします。
reader.en: Yes, please pay here.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: ありがとうございます。
reader.en: Thank you.

sourceEnglish.objective: combine entering, ordering, a restriction, a correction, small talk, and payment from lessons 1–14 in one ordinary morning
sourceEnglish.roleplay: Handle a routine café breakfast from greeting to payment, including one small mix-up, without English.
englishWordAnchors: Do you have a table for one?
Excuse me, I ordered oat milk.
Could you bring me the bill, please?
englishReading: First, I walked into the café and asked the waitress: Good morning, do you have a table for one?
She gave me a table near the counter.
Then I ordered an americano, scrambled eggs and toast.
I also told her: I can't have dairy, do you have oat milk?
When the coffee arrived, it had regular milk, and I told her: Excuse me, I ordered oat milk.
The waitress changed my coffee and asked me: Is this your first time in the city?
I answered: Yes, and afterward I'm going to visit the museum.
At the end I asked for the bill and paid by card.
Before leaving, I left a tip for the waitress.

lessons.title: Breakfast midpoint review
lessons.objective: Handle greeting, seating, order, a dairy restriction, an incorrect drink, and payment in one Japanese-led scene.
lessons.focus: This review combines earlier polite questions, order readback and bill terms. An allergy is not an ordinary substitution: if the wrong milk is used for an allergic guest, do not consume the drink or assume a remake is safe. Ask staff to verify ingredients and handling; decline if uncertain. English support remains available after reveal even though the speaking mission aims for Japanese.
lessons.scene: Sam, who avoids dairy, checks a breakfast order and finds the drink was made with regular milk.

cards.ja: 乳製品を避けています
原材料と扱い方を確認してください

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: おはようございます。一人です。席は空いていますか。
reader.en: Good morning. I am alone. Is a seat available?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい、こちらへどうぞ。
reader.en: Yes, please come this way.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: コーヒーとトーストをお願いします。乳製品を避けています。
reader.en: Coffee and toast, please. I avoid dairy.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: オーツミルクはありますか。
reader.en: Do you have oat milk?

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: はい。コーヒーに入れますか。
reader.en: Yes. Would you like it in your coffee?

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: お願いします。注文を確認してください。
reader.en: Yes, please. Please confirm the order.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: コーヒーはオーツミルクですね。
reader.en: The coffee is with oat milk.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: すみません。このコーヒーは牛乳のようです。飲みません。
reader.en: Excuse me. This coffee appears to have regular milk. I will not drink it.

reader.speaker: Staff
reader.ja: 確認します。少々お待ちください。
reader.en: I will check. Please wait a moment.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: ありがとうございます。確認できなければ、飲み物は注文しません。
reader.en: Thank you. If it cannot be verified, I will not order a drink.

reader.speaker: Sam
reader.ja: トーストのお会計をお願いします。カードで払えますか。
reader.en: The bill for the toast, please. Can I pay by card?
